practice: Some local agencies let finders care for a found pet at home under set conditions instead of bringing it in. LA Animal Services' Shelter-at-Home program allows home care for up to 30 days if the finder notifies a center, sends photos and has the animal scanned for a microchip within four hours. Montgomery County, Maryland, accepts either the animal itself or a found report, and says many animals are reunited by matching lost and found reports.

duty-to-report.value: Set by county or city law, so it varies. For example, Baltimore County, Maryland, requires a found report within 24 hours and handing the animal to county Animal Services within 72 hours; San Diego County, California, says by law you must notify county Animal Services and give a found dog to a shelter (County Code 62.676).

report-to.value: The local city or county animal services agency. For example, Montgomery County, Maryland, takes found reports online, in person or by phone at (240) 773-5900; LA Animal Services has finders notify the closest of its centers.

foster-yourself.value: Depends on the place. The City of Los Angeles allows home care for up to 30 days under its Shelter-at-Home rules, and Montgomery County, Maryland, allows it if you file a found report. Baltimore County, Maryland, requires the animal be turned over within 72 hours, and San Diego County says the only legal way to keep a found dog is to adopt it from County Animal Services.

owner-proof.value: Set by each shelter. For example, Montgomery County, Maryland, asks for at least one of license and vaccination records, purchase or adoption receipts, microchip registration documents or vet records, in a name matching your ID. LA Animal Services asks for proof such as photos, vaccination records or adoption certificates plus government-issued photo ID; Baltimore County, Maryland, also requires proof of current rabies vaccination.
